title: Observability-driven rollback and synthetic surge playbook for kernel-selection regressions
creator: Aisha Patel
description: After a capacity event on 2026-02-25 we observed a persistent p95 latency uplift attributable to suboptimal kernel selection under mixed quantization workloads. This ticket defines an observability-first rollback/playbook and synthetic surge harness to detect and contain future regressions quickly, plus concrete follow-ups for fixing telemetry blind spots and automating safe rollbacks.
incident_summary: During a regional capacity rebalancing window, the scheduler began routing a subset of traffic to a newer kernel candidate. Over ~90 minutes this produced a reproducible p95 latency increase for affected model families (open-llm/gpt-short-16k). Customers on Dedicated pools experienced increased tail latency and several timeouts. Manual mitigation involved pinning traffic to the previous kernel version and throttling probe frequency.
root_cause: Kernel candidate scoring decay combined with inadequate per-microbatch KV cache telemetry. The scheduler's probe heuristics allowed a candidate with poorer microbatch throughput to ramp because our rollout gates only tracked p50/p90 at the route level and not per-quantization-path microbatch metrics.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use the synthetic surge harness (scripts/harnesses/surge_v2.py) to replay mixed-quantization traffic (int8 + fp16) with sequence length distribution matching customer X (provided in testdata/seq_dist_customerX.json).
2) Enable candidate routing to 10% of traffic and run for 60–90 minutes while collecting kernel_score, microbatch_size_histogram, and kv_cache_hit_by_key for the worker group.
3) Observe p95 tail increases in Grafana dashboard 'runtime/kernel-selection/p95-by-quant' and correlate with per-microbatch KV hit ratio drop under the new candidate.
4) Verify that pinning kernel_version to previous stable candidate reduces p95 within 5 minutes.
mitigations_taken: Emergency pin of model family open-llm/gpt-short-16k to kernel:v1.13 for all affected Dedicated pools (rollout id: rb-20260225-01).
Reduced scheduler probe frequency from 3 probes/min -> 1 probe/min for canary candidates pending telemetry enrichment.
Applied temporary admission control to limit speculative candidate traffic to 5% of route concurrency.
action_items: (A1) Add per-microbatch telemetry: emit microbatch_size, kv_hit_ratio, and kernel_score per sample to the kernel_event stream (owner: Tomás, estimate: 3).
(A2) Implement a canary gate that enforces per-quant-path SLO checks (p95 and kv_hit_ratio) before increasing candidate weight beyond 5% (owner: Claire, estimate: 5).
(A3) Build an automated rollback playbook that triggers when a canary candidate violates per-quant-path p95 or kv_hit_ratio for two consecutive 15m windows (owner: SRE team, estimate: 3).
(A4) Create a synthetic surge harness in CI that runs as part of nightly smoke for top-10 models; fail the build if candidate score shows >15% p95 regression (owner: Eng QA, estimate: 4).
(A5) Enhance runbook docs: document manual triage steps, dashboard links, and safe pinning commands; include 'how to replicate with harness' section (owner: Aisha, estimate: 2).

(A6) Add alerting rule in Grafana/Alertmanager for 'kernel-selection-per-quant-p95' that triggers at warning (10% regression) and critical (20% regression) thresholds (owner: Observability team, estimate: 1).
(A7) Post-deploy calibrations: schedule a 2-week observation window after kernel releases with automated drift detection (owner: Release Eng, estimate: 2).
telemetry_changes: Emit microbatch-level metrics into kernel_event kafka topic with schema version v2 (fields: job_id, kernel_version, microbatch_size, kv_hit_ratio, quantization_path, p50/p90/p95 windows).
Tag existing route-level p95 metrics with quantization_path label to allow breaking down by fp16/int8/mixed.
Add structured logs for probe decisions including feature contributions to kernel_score (to aid ML model interpretations of scoring drift).
rollout_plan: Canary rollout protocol: 1) release kernel candidate behind feature flag; 2) route deterministic token sequences to candidate at 1% for 30m while collecting microbatch metrics; 3) if no regression, increase to 5% for 2h and run synthetic surge harness; 4) only increase beyond 5% after automated gate passes two consecutive windows. If gate fails at any point, automatically pin traffic back to previous stable kernel and page the oncall.
